title: Barbara Kruger

description.main: Rizzoli's 2010 monograph on Barbara Kruger, made with the artist, with an introduction by Hal Foster, essays by Alexander Alberro, Martha Gever, Miwon Kwon and Carol Squiers, and texts by Kruger.
description.extended:
Published by Rizzoli in 2010 and made in collaboration with the artist, this 307-page hardcover covers some thirty years of Barbara Kruger's work, including many pieces not previously published.

Hal Foster's introduction, "Seriously Playful," opens the book. The contents are arranged in sections on exterior installations, interior installations, publications and commodities, and flatworks, ending with an exhibition history. Essays sit between the sections. Miwon Kwon writes on "A Message from Barbara Kruger: Empathy Can Change the World," Martha Gever on the video installation Twelve, Alexander Alberro on images, text and social engagement, and Carol Squiers on Kruger's years at Mademoiselle. Kruger contributes four texts of her own: "Irony/Passion," "Work and Money," "Decadism" and "Utopia: The Promise of Fashion When Time Stands Still."

The book gives full spreads to Kruger's large-scale works and public projects, which take on abortion, consumerism, spirituality and identity.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American artist who pairs found photographs with declarative text. She worked as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, including Mademoiselle, before turning to photocollage in the late 1970s. She received the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the 51st Venice Biennale in 2005.

Size 9.5 x 11.75 in per photo-eye; library records give 31 cm. Publication date given as April 2010 (Amazon UK) and June 2010 (Rizzoli Bookstore).
